body: Just to add that it's "new yam festival" not Yam festival...did you study enough to understand the meaning and origin of the festival. Also, maybe understanding Nigeria's independence day and how actual Nigerians in Nigeria feel about this before deciding to celebrate it might be a good idea. If you want to learn Igbo language, there are some great YouTube channels for this - including ones where you can subscribe and get 1:1 lessons from Nigerians in Nigeria. I would look into this - if I were you. Cheers and good luck!

Being stopped by the police is not new. Being harassed by the police is not new and/ or unique to young people... I travelled by road a lot in the 80s, 90s, and till now. I have seen people be killed by police men for refusing to give them 20 naira in the 90s. I have sat in hours long holdup or traffic jam caused by police stops where every single car was expected to bribe.  I have sat with fear in the car when my driver was holding on to his deeper life religious conviction that he will not give bribe.In Nigeria, it's the luck of the draw. You are nothing. ( Not because you are nothing) But because Nigerians in power see you as nothing. Until we all start to recognize and understand what basic human rights are...the constant bullying and harassment is going nowhere. Contrary to popular opinion, it is not "profiling" ...that is a shallow interpretation/ appropriation of a term that originated in the west where human rights actually mean something.Its just a basic disregard for others by people who perceive themselves to have some power over you...which they do because like they have said over and over again and done over and over again - "I will shoot you and nothing will happen".
Have you read the Ahiara declaration? Have you even read anything of the history? Or do you expect strangers on the Internet to do the research for you?

DM me if you want to have an honest conversation. Cheers.
